paper_metadata.title: Enhanced fill probability estimates in institutional algorithmic bond trading using statistical learning algorithms with quantum computers

experiments.description: Projected quantum feature map (PQFM) generation using a Heisenberg-ansatz circuit on a noiseless quantum simulator, then using the generated features in classical fill-probability models for corporate bond RFQ backtesting.

algorithm.variant: Projected Quantum Feature Map (PQFM) with Heisenberg ansatz, noiseless simulation

hyperparameters.measurement_observables: 1-local Pauli observables (X, Y, Z on each qubit)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 216 normalized classical event features are encoded into a 109-qubit Heisenberg-style circuit; the paper states that one block corresponds to two repetitions/trotter steps, and the PQFM outputs 3N = 327 features from 1-local Pauli measurements.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Generate transformed market-state features x' = $M(U_alpha(x)|b0>) to improve downstream fill-probability estimation.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Heisenberg Hamiltonian with pairwise terms J_j [X_j X_{j+1} + Y_j Y_{j+1} + 2 Z_j Z_{j+1}] and Trotterized unitary evolution.

problem_instance.description: Real intraday corporate bond RFQ market-state vectors transformed by a quantum feature map and then evaluated in classical backtesting.
problem_instance.dataset_name: HSBC intraday corporate bond RFQ dataset

dataset_specification.description: European corporate bond market; trading period Sep 1, 2023 to Oct 29, 2024; active window Jul 24, 2024 onward; 69 trading days in active window; 143,912 RFQs in active window; 3,425 bonds; 652 tickers; 216 numerical event features; features scaled to [-1, 1] after normalization and tanh transform; 16,000 events randomly sampled for quantum feature generation; backtesting uses rolling time windows and blinding windows up to 4 trading days.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Normalize features with z-score scaling, then apply 2r * tanh(1/3) to reduce outliers and fit quantum rotation range; discretize normalized feature values into bins for event matching when used.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Backtesting with out-of-sample AUC; rolling training window; cross-validation on random subsets within the training period; test on future RFQs with varying blinding windows.

hardware.device_name: Qiskit Aer / Matrix Product State simulator

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Feature normalization, z-score scaling, tanh compression, event matching/binning when applicable.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical machine-learning models trained on PQFM outputs; evaluation by AUC backtesting.

speedup_claims.caveats: No computational speedup is reported for the noiseless simulator experiment; only predictive performance (AUC) is evaluated.

experiments.description: Classical-quantum event matching (CQEM) experiment reusing PQFM features from the longer Heisenberg circuit on ibm_torino to decouple labels and test fill-probability estimation on unseen trade instances.

algorithm.variant: Classical-quantum event matching with PQFM feature reuse

hyperparameters.measurement_observables: 1-local Pauli observables (X, Y, Z on each qubit), with some 2-local observables included in some cases

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical event vectors are discretized into K identifiers using uniform binning over [-1, 1]; PQFM features are generated for a subset of events and then reused for other events sharing the same K. The paper states that this can represent up to (Nbins)^216 theoretical market states.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Reuse quantum-generated features for unseen but similar classical events while reducing direct label leakage and testing whether fill-probability estimation remains improved.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Label independence enforced by matching on discretized event identifiers K and reusing PQFM vectors for events with the same K.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Heisenberg Hamiltonian underlying the PQFM generator.

problem_instance.description: Out-of-sample fill-probability estimation on future RFQs using event-matched PQFM features, excluding the 16k training events used to generate the matched quantum features.
problem_instance.dataset_name: HSBC intraday corporate bond RFQ dataset

dataset_specification.description: Same dataset as the main experiment; 16,000 PQFM training events from the active window are excluded, leaving 127,912 events for matching; matching uses the full active trading window and future RFQs; best reported performance at 97% matching resolution and no blinding.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Preprocessed and scaled dataset; discretize each feature into Nbins bins over [-1, 1]; construct K identifiers; match K values between generated PQFM sample and unseen events; aggregate matched PQFM vectors with mean function.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Backtesting with out-of-sample AUC under varying blinding windows and event-matching resolutions; compare classical-input and quantum-generated-input models.

noise_model.noise_type: device noise on IBM Heron r1 processor
noise_model.mitigation_details: Same hardware execution and mitigation as the longer PQFM experiment; CQEM reuses generated PQFM features and applies mean aggregation over matched identifiers.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Feature normalization, z-score scaling, tanh compression, discretization into bins, K-grouped matching, mean aggregation of matched PQFM vectors.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical machine-learning models trained on event-matched PQFM outputs; evaluation by AUC backtesting.

speedup_claims.caveats: CQEM is evaluated on predictive performance only. The paper reports a best mean test AUC of 0.89±0.02 at 97% matching resolution and no blinding, but no computational speedup.
